title: Kejriwal Escalates E20 Fight With National Town Hall and Petition March to PM Modi
excerpt: AAP leader announces August 1 town hall at Constitution Club, plans to deliver two lakh public petitions to PM Modi's residence demanding E20 rollback.
body:
• AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal announced a 'National Town Hall Against E20' at New Delhi's Constitution Club on August 1, open to in-person and online participation.
  • Kejriwal plans to deliver more than two lakh citizen petitions to PM Modi's residence demanding a rollback of the E20 ethanol-blended petrol policy.
  • Delhi transport unions have separately called a protest march to Parliament on August 4, demanding the withdrawal of mandatory ethanol blending.
  • The escalation follows Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and growing public anger over vehicle damage and lower mileage from E20 fuel.

Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has announced a 'National Town Hall Against E20' to be held at the Constitution Club of India in New Delhi on August 1, marking a sharp escalation in the political battle over India's ethanol-blended petrol policy. Kejriwal said more than two lakh petitions collected from citizens would be delivered to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence in the days following the event.

Town Hall and Transport Union Protests

Addressing a press conference on July 27, Kejriwal invited residents of Delhi-NCR to attend in person while those from other states could join online via a registration number. The event will bring together experts, affected vehicle owners and the general public to discuss concerns about E20 fuel — a blend of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol that India has rolled out nationwide.

"We are starting a National Town Hall this Saturday afternoon to unite people on this issue. Through this Town Hall, we will hold discussions with experts, victims, and the general public."

— Arvind Kejriwal, AAP National Convenor

Separately, Delhi-based transport bodies have announced a protest march to Parliament on August 4, demanding the complete withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol. The Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association, the All India Motor Transport Congress, and the All India Motor & Goods Transport Association are coordinating the march.

"We want to give a wake-up call to the members of Parliament who are sleeping on this issue," said Sanjay Samrat, president of the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters Association. Harish Sabharwal of the All India Motor Transport Congress added that ethanol-blended petrol "should not be forced upon commuters" and consumers should have a choice.

The E20 Controversy

The nationwide E20 rollout has faced mounting public resistance over claims of reduced vehicle mileage, engine damage and higher effective fuel costs. Kejriwal has repeatedly alleged the Centre's policy amounts to an "experiment" on 140 crore people, pointing to the government's own submission in the Supreme Court that described the blending programme as experimental.

The AAP leader earlier wrote to PM Modi seeking an appointment to discuss the issue and demanded that fuel stations offer both pure petrol and E20, with lower prices for the blended variant. An online petition launched by the party has gathered over two lakh signatures.

The controversy has spawned online movements, including the 'E-20 Janata Party' — formed along the lines of the 'Cockroach Janata Party' that emerged during student protests — which has rapidly accumulated followers on Instagram and X.

Political Stakes After Pradhan Exit

Kejriwal's escalation comes on the heels of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, which the AAP leader credited to sustained youth pressure. He warned that the E20 issue could trigger similarly large-scale nationwide unrest if left unaddressed.

"The youth of this country have made an arrogant government bow down, resulting in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Now, I request the Prime Minister to also resolve the E20 issue before it turns into a massive protest."

— Arvind Kejriwal, AAP National Convenor

The government has defended the E20 programme, ruling out any immediate plan to increase blending beyond 20 per cent and asserting that the fuel is safe, supports clean energy goals and benefits farmers. Kejriwal has also criticised the police lathi-charge on student protesters at Jantar Mantar, accusing the Modi government of "extreme arrogance" in suppressing peaceful dissent.

What Comes Next

The August 1 town hall is expected to serve as a launchpad for broader mobilisation. With transport unions marching to Parliament three days later and the online petition count rising, the E20 debate appears set to become one of the defining political flashpoints of the monsoon session. For diaspora Indians with vehicles and property in India, the fuel policy's economic impact on transportation costs and vehicle maintenance adds a direct financial dimension to the controversy.
